newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese yuan ends up at intraday high vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Chinese yuan ends up at intraday high vs dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at an intraday high of 8.2905 on Thursday from Wednesday's 8.2919 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai due to speculative buying in the last few minutes of trading, traders said.
The weighted average price on Wednesday was 8.2919.
The yuan opened higher at 8.2915 and hit an intraday low of 8.2916 early in trading.
It then moved in a narrow range of 8.2910 and 8.2915 for most of the session before speculative buying in the last few minutes pushed it to a high at the close, traders said.
Trading was dull with most business done at about 8.2913.

One dealer said pro-yuan sentiment was strong on the market on an oversupply of U.S. dollars due to China's heavy foreign trade surplus, continued inflow of foreign invesment and rising foreign exchange reserves.
But the yuan was already at a high level and was unlikely to move sharply in the short term without fresh stimuli, he said.
A second dealer said speculative buying and selling had pushed the yuan sharply up and down over the past few weeks.
"But the speculative acts have only involved a little money and cannot represent the market trend," he said.
Traders said they expected the yuan to move in a narrow range of 8.2900 and 8.2910 on Friday.
The yuan closed up at 7.1431 from 7.1800 against 100 Japanese yen and down at an intraday low of 1.0710 from 1.0702 against the Hong Kong dollar.
